brief: A weak September payrolls print (29k vs 90k consensus) cut Fed October hike odds below 20%, pushing the S&P +73bps to 7723 even as the 10yr held at 5.27%; GS itself sees an October hike as unlikely and a strong chance the FOMC concludes no further hikes are needed. The Pentagon is sending a third carrier group and 10k troops to the Persian Gulf, and Tehran is preparing a broader response to any renewed large-scale US attack, with Brent back near $102. US hedge fund net leverage fell a third straight week to 46.4%, near 5-year lows, while Europe saw its largest net equity buying in over five years. Consensus S&P Q3 EPS growth is 27% y/y, but AI infrastructure spend drives over half of it and the top 10 stocks, led by Micron and Nvidia at 34%, supply 68% of that growth (vs 48% in Q2) as the median stock grows only ~9%, pushing breadth to its weakest since the dot-com bubble. GS also flags a GSXUBOND duration basket (RSI<30, yield>4%) as a tactical long or hedge, and reports an Amazon Conviction List add plus unrelated EU stock-list changes, chip pricing, and gold-discovery items without elaboration.
